To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
we sequenced the completely pNAH20 plasmid and found that it is a derivative of the previously sequenced plasmid pCAR1.
the completely sequenced pNAH20 naphthalene-degradation plasmid from the multiplasmid P. fluorescense strain PC20 is a potential bioremediation tool.
The naphthalene degrader P. fluorescns PC20 harbors two plasmids, one of which is completely sequenced, pNAH20.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the molecular analysis of naphthalene degrader Pseudomonas species and their plasmids.
the complete nucleotide sequence of plasmid pCAR1 from Pseudomonads and with the complete nucleotides sequences of the two naphthalene-degrading plasmids, pDTG1 and pNAH20.
the molecular mechanisms that govern conjugal transfer of the NAH plasmid pCAR1 and its derivatives.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
pNAH20 represents a novel IncP-9 NAH plasmid, which is a member of the pCAR family.
the two plasmid systems are very similar but not identical.
the two plasmid pCAR1 and pNAH20 have evolved in a different manner and have different properties.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the two NAH plasmids, pNAH20 and pDTG1 are highly related but have different functions.
we have completed the first step of the pNAH20 sequencing project and have provided a detailed analysis of the plasmid structure.
we have completed the sequencing of pNAH7, pNAH20 and pDTG1 and that we have shown that the plasmids can be mobilized to the soil environment.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the plasmid backbone is more important than the catabolic genes for plasmid mobilization and transfer.
the plasmid backbone and the catabolic genes are not always linked together in a stable manner.
the naphthalene catabolic gene cluster is a hot-spot for IS element insertion and that this can lead to significant changes in plasmid transfer capacity.
